findings.title: Runbook describes kill switch as operational control; code only logs
signals_cited: docs/runbook.md stale 272 days behind the code

evidence.quote:
`payments.killswitch` in `internal/flags/flags.go` is a permanent operational
kill switch. It is off in normal operation and is flipped by on-call during an
incident; do not remove it as dead code.

findings.note: Runbook tells on-call this is an operational kill switch that stops payments during an incident. The only code reading it logs a line; no payment-processing code exists anywhere in the repo for it to gate.

findings.title: No CHANGELOG or CONTRIBUTING despite two tagged releases

evidence.quote:
# app

Go service with a lookup table, a string dispatcher and a fluent builder.

findings.note: Repository has tagged releases v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 but no CHANGELOG.md, no CONTRIBUTING.md, and no ADR directory recording design decisions such as the builder TLS option or the kill switch.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: Flagged as 533 days stale, but its generic description (lookup table, string dispatcher, fluent builder) still accurately matches internal/lookup, internal/dispatch and internal/build as currently written; no contradicting claim found.
Flagged as 272 days stale, but the flag name, file path, and default value it documents (internal/flags/flags.go, payments.killswitch=false) still match the code exactly.

not_assessed: Whether payment-processing logic gated by this flag exists in another repository/service not present here
Whether the commented-out lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml reflects a documented CI policy elsewhere
